details: The simulator compares recurring investment rules with the same contributed cash. Read the displayed data dates and assumptions before interpreting an outcome.

title: My Travel
blurb: Compare complete journeys and reservations using your available tools, then verify bookings within your authorisation.
requirements: A compatible agent harness and suitable travel/search tools or authorised browser sessions. The skill does not bundle a booking engine or account access.
details: Considers dates, airports, cabins, loyalty options, stopovers and ground transport against the user’s requirements. Challenges the preferred itinerary and checks the completed booking and usable benefits.
Synthetic decision checks cover planning rules; they do not establish that a live fare is available or that a booking has succeeded.

title: myrepo
blurb: Publish a project to GitHub with a Pages site, a preview, privacy and secret checks, and live-URL verification.
requirements: Node.js and GitHub CLI with your existing OAuth login. Public publishing follows your approval and a dry-run preview.
details: Publishes browser-ready projects, or provides a landing page for projects that need local software. Preserves existing documentation by default.
Checks publishable files and the Git history being introduced for secrets and machine-specific paths. Its offline self-test checks safety gates separately from GitHub account readiness.

title: myvoice
blurb: Consented local F5-TTS voice cloning in Promptus, with signal, word-accuracy and human listening checks.
requirements: Windows, the Promptus desktop app and the documented local F5-TTS workflow. Use your own voice or a speaker’s explicit permission.
details: myvoice is the short callable name for promptus-clone-voice. Follow the full canonical protocol linked below.
Generation is local. Reference admission, signal and word checks, and a recorded human listening verdict precede acceptance. Label shared cloned speech as synthetic.

title: myautoness
blurb: Solve repeatable games or UI tasks using bounded search, observation and verified replay.
requirements: A compatible agent harness and either a deterministic simulation adapter or working browser/UI controls. The portable self-test does not itself play a game.
details: Uses classical search and planning, seeded exploration and verified input traces. It does not train a neural network. “autopilot” is its legacy alias.
A lesson is saved only after clean-start replay verifies success against the same engine and content. Observation mode first checks control, visibility, coherent observations and a clear outcome.

title: myskills
blurb: Check the five executable skill families and report functional health separately from local dependency readiness.
requirements: Node.js and the sibling skills collection. Live dependency probes depend on installed CLIs, account sessions and local Promptus services.
details: Checks MOMM, myrepo, myautoness, yorkshire-pudding/yorky and promptus-clone-voice/myvoice. Aliases belong to their canonical family; My Travel is outside this executable health suite.
Quick mode skips live probes and marks those dependencies not checked. Passing code checks do not mean every required service is ready.

title: yorky
blurb: Translate prose into Yorkshire dialect at three strengths while preserving code identifiers, URLs and logic.
requirements: A compatible agent harness; Node.js for the bundled deterministic prose translator. Code translation follows the skill’s protected-zone rules.
details: yorky is the short callable name for yorkshire-pudding. Choose mild, proper or broad dialect.
The prose tool and the agent’s code-editing protocol are distinct: identifiers, keys, URLs, placeholders and program behaviour must remain intact.

title: Promptus Media Lab
blurb: React editing-cue workspace that uses Gemini to draft dialogue, audio, visual and effect markers for a timeline.
requirements: Node.js for local development and your own configured Gemini access for AI cue generation. Provider use may incur charges.
details: The public repository named 42 contains this Media Lab application. It is separate from the 42.uk website catalog and from 42 MOMM Diffusion.

The app uses React, TypeScript and Vite, with Gemini for structured editing cues and ffmpeg.wasm for browser media handling. This is an editing-cue workspace, not a claim of automatic finished-video generation.
